hooks.prompt: Decide whether Claude may stop. Answer ok: true unless the assistant's latest response completed a unit of work substantial enough to log to MEMORY.md (a shipped feature, a resolved bug, a meaningful decision, an approach that took more than two attempts) and no MEMORY.md entry has been proposed for that work yet. One-line answers, clarifying questions, information lookups, interrupted thoughts, trivial work, and responses that already propose an entry are always ok: true. Be conservative — frequent low-value proposals are noise. When logging is warranted, answer ok: false with this reason: 'Do NOT write to MEMORY.md yet. Draft the one-block entry and surface it to the user with a short note like "Worth logging to MEMORY.md? Reply 'log it' to record this entry:" followed by the drafted block. Only invoke the decision-log skill to write once the user confirms.' Rationale: an unconfirmed, model-generated memory entry becomes context the agent reads every future session, and machine-generated context measurably degrades agent performance; a human-confirmed entry does not. (To restore the old silent-append behavior, replace that reason with 'Invoke the decision-log skill to append the entry.' — see README, 'Tune the Stop hook'.)
